## CPI Aerostructures Reports Third Quarter and Nine Month 2026 Results


November 16, 2026


**Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025**


- Revenue of $20.0 million compared to $19.3 million;
- Gross profit of $4.6 million compared to $4.3 million;
- Gross margin of 23.1% compared to 22.3%;
- Net income of $1.3 million compared to $1.1 million;
- Earnings per share of $0.10 compared to earnings per share of $0.09;
- Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $2.1 million compared to $1.9 million.


**Nine Months 2026 vs. Nine Months 2025**


- Revenue of $54.9 million compared to $49.8 million;
- Gross profit of $13.0 million compared to $6.6 million;
- Gross margin of 23.6% compared to 13.3% (20.4% excluding A-10 Program impact(2));
- Net income of $3.2 million compared to net (loss) of $(1.5) million;
- Earnings per share of $0.25 compared to (loss) per share of $(0.12);
- Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $5.5 million compared to $(0.6) million ($3.9 million excluding A-10 Program impact).


EDGEWOOD, N.Y., Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- CPI Aerostructures, Inc. ("CPI Aero" or the "Company") (NYSE American: CVU) today reported financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, highlighted by continued revenue growth, significant profitability improvements, and expanding margins.


The Company's performance reflects increasing throughput, strong execution across key Aerospace & Defense programs, and ongoing operational discipline. For the first nine months of 2026, CPI Aero nearly doubled gross profit, returned to solid profitability, and delivered substantial growth in Adjusted EBITDA compared to the prior-year period.


"Our 2026 performance continues to demonstrate the strength of our operating strategy and the dedication of our team," said Dorith Hakim, President and Chief Executive Officer of CPI Aero. "Through the first nine months of the year, we achieved revenue growth, significant margin expansion, improving cash flows and meaningful increases in profitability. Gross profit increased by $6.3 million year over year, while net income improved by $4.8 million, reflecting the benefits of a stronger product mix, disciplined program execution, and continued operational efficiency improvements."


Ms. Hakim continued, "Demand across our core defense platforms remains robust, and our ability to execute consistently for our customers positions us well for continued growth. Our Adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million underscores the strength of the business and remains strong even after normalizing for the impact of the A-10 program on prior year results."


"With backlog at approximately $634 million up from $505 million at year end 2025, which includes awards received this year of $70 million supporting next-generation defense platforms, we enter the final months of 2026 with strong visibility and confidence. We remain focused on executing our programs safely, efficiently, and with the highest quality standards while continuing to create long-term value for our shareholders. Based on the strength of our backlog and customer demand, we believe CPI Aero is well positioned to maintain its positive momentum into 2027."


**About CPI Aero**


CPI Aero is a prime contractor to the U.S. Department of War as well as a Tier 1 subcontractor to some of the largest aerospace and defense contractors in the world. CPI Aero provides engineering, program management, supply chain management, assembly operations and MRO services to this global network of customers. CPI Aero is recognized as a leader within the international aerospace market in such areas as aircraft structural assemblies, military advanced tactical pod structures, engine air inlets, and complex welded products.


Our OEM customers in the defense sector include (i) Lockheed Martin Corporation and Sikorsky Aircraft, for the F-16 Fighting Falcon, the UH-60 BLACK HAWK©, the MH-60 Seahawk, the CH-53E and the CH-53K King Stallion; (ii) RTX Corporation, formerly Raytheon Technologies Corporation, for the ALQ-249 Next Generation Jammer Mid-Band Pod for the EA-18G Growlers, the Advanced Tactical Pods, the MS-110 & TacSAR Reconnaissance Airborne Pods, Hypersonic Missile Wings, and B-52 Radar Modernization; (iii) L3Harris for the Next Generation Jammer Low-Band Pod for the EA-18G Growlers; (iv) Collins Aerospace, for RF Enclosures; (v) Northrop Grumman Corporation, for the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye, the Airborne Laser Mine Detection Pod, welded tubes, aerial refueling probes, and welded fluid tanks; and (vi) the DOD/USAF and the Defense Logistics Agency for the T-38 Pacer Classic and T-38 Talon. Our OEM customers in the civil aviation market include Embraer S.A. for the Phenom 300 and Phenom 100.


Our funded backlog of remaining performance obligations exceeds $106 million and the unfunded backlog of future orders for the expected duration of existing programs is $528 million. Our total backlog is $634 million.

**Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Measures**


Note: (1) Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure defined as GAAP net income (loss) adjusted for provision (benefit) for income taxes, interest expense, depreciation, stock-based compensation expense and other income/ expenses. Adjusted EBITDA excluding the A-10 adjustment is a non-GAAP measure defined as Adjusted EBITDA further adjusted to exclude the $4,468,528 A-10 program adjustment recorded in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


We have provided Adjusted EBITDA because we believe it is a commonly used measure of financial performance among comparable companies and helps investors evaluate operating results on a consistent basis. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered a substitute for GAAP cash flows as a measure of liquidity. The adjustments to calculate this non-GAAP financial measure and the basis for such adjustments are outlined below. Please refer to the following table below that reconciles GAAP net income (loss) to Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA excluding the A-10 adjustment.


We have also provided Adjusted EBITDA excluding the A-10 adjustment to enhance understanding of our operating results and facilitate comparisons between periods by separately identifying the impact of the A-10 program adjustment on the prior-year results. This measure should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP net income (loss), and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies.


The adjustments used to calculate Adjusted EBITDA are described below:


*Provision (benefit) for income taxes.* Relates to our estimated federal and state corporate income tax liabilities or credits for the period.


*Interest expense.* Relates to the interest incurred under our bank credit facilities.


*Depreciation* . The Company incurs depreciation expense (recorded in cost of sales and in selling, general and administrative expenses) related to capital assets purchased, leased or constructed to support the ongoing operations of the business. The assets are recorded at cost and are depreciated over the estimated useful lives of individual assets.


*Stock-based compensation expense* . The Company incurs non-cash expense related to stock-based compensation included in its GAAP presentation of cost of sales and selling, general and administrative expenses. Management believes that exclusion of these expenses allows comparison of operating results to those of other companies that disclose non-GAAP financial measures that exclude stock-based compensation.


*Other income/ expenses* . Includes amounts that are one time in nature/non-recurring, primarily representing forgiven payables.


Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for financial information provided in accordance with GAAP. This non-GAAP financial measure may not be computed in the same manner as similarly titled measures used by other companies. The Company expects to continue to incur expenses similar to the Adjusted EBITDA financial adjustments described above, and investors should not infer from the Company's presentation of this non-GAAP financial measure that these costs are unusual, infrequent, or non-recurring.

Note (2) Gross margin excluding the A-10 Program impact is a non-GAAP financial measure. For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, GAAP gross margin was 13.3%, calculated as GAAP gross profit of $6,619,171 divided by GAAP revenue of $49,848,818. Excluding the A-10 program adjustment adds back $4,468,528 to both gross profit and revenue, resulting in non-GAAP gross profit of $11,087,699 and non-GAAP revenue of $54,317,346. Dividing these adjusted gross profit and revenue amounts results in gross margin excluding the A-10 Program impact of 20.4%.


We have provided this measure to enhance understanding of our operating results and facilitate comparisons between periods by separately identifying the impact of the A-10 program adjustment on the prior-year results.
